newsitem.title: USA: Eastman Kodak to slash 4,000 jobs worldwide.
newsitem.headline: Eastman Kodak to slash 4,000 jobs worldwide.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co will cut 4,000 jobs worldwide in the next 12 to 18 months, a company spokesman said late on Thursday in a telephone interview.

"These will probably be layoffs of one sort or another," Kodak spokesman Paul Allen said, when asked if the cuts would be done through attrition. Earlier Kodak reported fourth quarter earnings which included a $256 million restructuring charge.
Allen said most of the job cuts would be outside the United States but added that the company did not have a specific breakdown of where the cuts would occur.

He said new hiring in areas of the business that are growing would more than likely offset the cuts and that the company's employment should remain level. Kodak had 96,000 employees at year-end 1995, he said.

The fourth quarter restructuring charge was taken to account for the job cuts. Earlier, Kodak posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.49 per share on revenue of $4.4 billion. Excluding restructuring charges, earnings were $1.19 per share.
Wall Street analysts generally expected the company's fourth quarter earnings to be around $1.12 per share. Kodak stock closed on Thursday up 4-1/4 at 85-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange.
